properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 while root-causing Alex's `content`-only report. **reflow2 returns `structuredContent` on every JSON tool and declares `outputSchema` on NONE of them.**

    grep -rniE 'output_schema|outputSchema' --include=*.rs crates/   ->  no matches
    rmcp 3.1.2 src/model/tool.rs:30  pub output_schema: Option<Arc<JsonObject>>
    rmcp 3.1.2 src/model/tool.rs:210 with_raw_output_schema(...)
    rmcp 3.1.2 src/model/tool.rs:242 with_output_schema::<T>()

So the SDK offers the field with two builders, `input_schema` is populated for all ~165 tools, and `output_schema` is left `None` everywhere. MCP pairs `outputSchema` with `structuredContent`: the schema is what tells a client what the structured payload will look like and, on the client side, whether to expect one at all.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A CANDIDATE CAUSE FOR THE FIELD REPORT. `dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer` framed the outage as *the client does not read `structuredContent`* and listed five things to do about it, all remediation. None asked whether reflow2 gives a client grounds to read it. A client that surfaces the structured payload only for tools advertising an output contract would behave EXACTLY as Alex describes against this server, while negotiating the newest protocol revision — which is the combination the decision found hardest to explain.

🛑 IT IS A CANDIDATE, NOT THE CAUSE, AND ONE MEASUREMENT ALREADY BOUNDS IT. Absence of `outputSchema` is NOT SUFFICIENT to cause the failure: `claude-code 2.1.241` reads this server's `structuredContent` without difficulty against the same undeclared surface, observed continuously through this session. So the claim can only ever be that the absence is NECESSARY for grok-shell specifically, not that it breaks clients in general. Anything stronger is unsupported.

⭐ THE DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT, AND IT IS SMALL: declare `output_schema` on ONE tool, ship it, have Alex call that tool and one undeclared one in the same session.
  • declared arrives, undeclared does not  ->  CAUSE CONFIRMED, and the repair is to declare output schemas rather than to choose among (b)–(e).
  • neither arrives  ->  REFUTED; the client ignores `structuredContent` unconditionally and the decision's remaining options stand unchanged.
Either result is worth the round-trip, and n=1 tool is enough because the two arms run against the same server in the same session.

🛑 AND THE FINDING STANDS ON ITS OWN EVEN IF THE EXPERIMENT REFUTES IT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED SEPARATELY FROM THE DECISION. reflow2's own doctrine says an undeclared contract can be neither honoured nor violated — `seam_report` exists to find exactly this, and the project treats an Interface with an empty spec as a defect shape. **The seam between reflow2 and every MCP client is declared on the input side for 165 tools and undeclared on the output side for all of them.** That asymmetry was never decided; it is what happens when `input_schema` is required by the SDK's constructor and `output_schema` is optional. Same class as the hand-maintained contract this project keeps finding: the field nobody was forced to fill.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: what a full declaration would cost. Tool outputs here are `serde_json::Value` built by hand rather than typed structs, so `with_output_schema::<T>()` has no `T` to name for most tools and `with_raw_output_schema` would mean writing schemas by hand or deriving types first. Nobody has priced it, and the one-tool experiment deliberately does not require pricing it.
